```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

A package's tests check that each version is consistent with itself. They do not
check what a user of the last release meets after upgrading: the code from the
vignettes and the help pages they learned from, run unchanged under the new version.
pkgdossier runs that code under both versions, each installed in its own library and
run in its own R process, and lists every difference with a mechanical label. It
does not decide whether a difference is intended; it gives you the evidence and the
NEWS bullets that might explain it.

## A first dossier

pkgdossier ships a tiny package, `udfixture`, in two versions with one planted
difference of each kind. `example_dossier()` describes a comparison of the two;
like `dossier()`, it only describes, and nothing is installed yet.

```{r}
library(pkgdossier)
d <- example_dossier()
d
```

`run_dossier()` runs the stages in turn: `prepare_versions()` installs both
versions into the work folder, `run_scenarios()` runs the scenarios four times
(baseline, candidate, candidate, baseline), and `compare_runs()` compares the runs.
It then writes the HTML report and the JSON. Each stage caches its work, so a second
call after changing the candidate rebuilds and reruns only the candidate.

```{r}
cmp <- run_dossier(d, html = file.path(tempdir(), "dossier-page"), open = FALSE, quiet = TRUE)
cmp
```

## Reading the differences

Each difference has one kind, with a severity for sorting: 1 for code that breaks
(a new error, a removed element), 2 for results that move, 3 for output, plots and
timing, 4 for additions and fixes. `unstable` (0) marks a step whose two runs under
one version disagree, so it cannot be compared.

`differences()` returns them as a data frame to filter:

```{r}
diffs <- differences(cmp, max_severity = 2)
diffs[, c("step", "kind", "path", "base", "cand")]
```

`summary()` has one row per step:

```{r}
s <- summary(cmp)
head(s[, c("scenario", "step", "status", "kinds", "news")], 10)
```

## NEWS candidates

For each step, pkgdossier reads the candidate's NEWS from the sections written after
the baseline's version and attaches the bullets that name a function the step uses.
A difference in a step that no bullet names gets `no_news = TRUE`: a change users
will meet that the NEWS may not tell them about.

```{r}
named <- differences(cmp, no_news = FALSE)
named[, c("step", "kind", "news")]
nrow(differences(cmp, no_news = TRUE))
```

This is a search, not a judgement: a bullet can name a function without covering the
change, and a change can be covered by a bullet in other words.

## Writing it up

The report (`write_dossier_html()`) is a folder that opens in any browser without a
network: provenance of both versions, the labelled differences, and per step the
side-by-side output, the numbers that moved and the plot pairs. `write_dossier_json()`
writes the same data as JSON. `write_dossier_md()` writes a short summary for a
pull-request comment:

```{r, results = "asis"}
cat(write_dossier_md(cmp))
```

The package ships a GitHub Actions workflow that runs a dossier of the CRAN release
against each pull request and posts this summary:
`system.file("github", "pkgdossier.yaml", package = "pkgdossier")`.

## Your own package

In your package's folder, one call makes the dossier:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
run_dossier()
```

It compares the folder with the package's CRAN release, running the release's
vignettes and help-page examples under both, and is the same as
`run_dossier(dossier("mypkg"))`: only the package's name is read from the folder.
It asks before downloading, opens the report, and prints the comparison, starting
with a one-line verdict. When it cannot start, it says why and what to write
instead: outside a package folder it names the package nearby; for a package not
on CRAN yet it names the repository's tags (`base = git_ref(".", "v0.3.0")`); for a
missing dependency it gives the `install.packages()` line. A step that hangs is
stopped after `step_timeout` (5 minutes for one execution) and recorded, and a step
that crashes R is recorded too. Call it again after a change: what has not changed is
reused, and only the candidate is rebuilt and rerun (its timings are then shown but
not labelled, as they were not made alongside the baseline's).

As a user of a package rather than its maintainer, compare the version you have
with the current release before upgrading:
`run_dossier(dossier("ggplot2", base = installed_version(), candidate = cran_release()))`.
A version installed from GitHub or R-universe has no CRAN source, and the call says
what to write instead.

To say more, describe the dossier: where both versions come from and which code to
run. Scenario files add code neither the vignettes nor the examples cover.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
d <- dossier("mypkg",
  base = cran_release(),                       # or cran_version("1.2.0"), tarball()
  candidate = git_ref("path/to/mypkg", "main"), # or local_path("path/to/mypkg")
  scenarios = list(from_vignettes(), from_examples(),
                   scenario_file("dev/dossier/scenarios.R")),
  work = file.path(tempdir(), "dossier-mypkg")
)
cmp <- run_dossier(d)
```

Everything that shapes the runs (`reps`, the seed, the console width, the
dependencies and so on) is set in `dossier()`, and `print(d)` shows it. The stages
take only how they run, such as `step_timeout` and `workers`, and `compare_runs()`
takes the tolerances: changing one only compares again. A setting given to the
wrong function is an error that writes out the right call, and `cmp$dossier` is
the dossier a comparison was made from.

A scenario file uses `scenario()` and `step()`. Steps in one scenario share an
environment, so later steps see what earlier steps created:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
scenario("basics", title = "Linear model", source = "README",
  step("setup", "setup", d <- head(mtcars, 20)),
  step("fit", "fit", fit <- lm(mpg ~ wt, data = d)),
  step("coef", "print", coef(fit), values = TRUE),
  step("plot", "plot", plot(d$wt, d$mpg), w = 5, h = 4)
)
```

By default both versions use the dependencies in your library, so differences come
from the package alone; `prepare_versions()` says before installing if a version
needs a dependency you do not have. With `dossier(..., deps = deps_cran())` it
instead installs the current CRAN versions of every dependency into the work folder,
as a new user installing today would get them, and with `deps_snapshot()` the
versions CRAN had when the baseline was released (see `?deps`). Downloads happen only in `prepare_versions()`, which
says what it fetches and asks first in an interactive session.
